<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518913771_theRebbe_98" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518913771_theRebbe_98__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the connection between the oath "be righteous" and Rosh Hashanah, based on the Alter Rebbe's discourse and the concept that every Jew contains a spark of Adam's soul, making Rosh Hashanah the birthday of every Jew.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing what our sages, of blessed memory, said:</t>
    <t s="2">"They administer an oath to him: 'Be righteous, etc.'"</t>
    <t s="3">And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, said</t>
    <t s="4">in the name of the Tzemach Tzedek,</t>
    <t s="5">that on the first Rosh Hashanah of his life</t>
    <t s="6">(the year 5550),</t>
    <t s="7">the Alter Rebbe delivered a discourse on "They administer an oath to him: 'Be righteous, etc.'"</t>
    <t s="8">And these are the first three chapters of the Tanya.</t>
    <t s="9">And one must explain the connection of the concept of "administering an oath to him" to Rosh Hashanah, based on what is explained in Likkutei Torah,</t>
    <t s="10">that this that each Jew is called "Adam"</t>
    <t s="11">("You are called Adam"),</t>
    <t s="12">is</t>
    <t s="13">because in the soul of each Jew there is a portion of the soul of Adam the First.</t>
    <t s="14">And from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="15">that on Rosh Hashanah</t>
    <t s="16">(the day when Adam the First was created),</t>
    <t s="17">when there is renewed</t>
    <t s="18">(each year)</t>
    <t s="19">the matter of the drawing down of the soul of Adam the First into his body</t>
    <t s="20">("And He blew</t>
    <t s="21">into his nostrils the soul of life"),</t>
    <t s="22">this is also the birthday of every Jew.</t>
    <t s="23">And it can be said that this is the connection of "administering an oath to him" to Rosh Hashanah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section connects the oath to the month of Tishrei, explaining that the phrase "the seventh month" has three meanings—simple seventh, oath, and satiety—paralleling the three interpretations of the oath.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this can be connected with the explanation of the Midrash</t>
    <t s="1">on the verse:</t>
    <t s="2">"In the seventh month, which is the month of oath"</t>
    <t s="3">(seventh from the word oath),</t>
    <t s="4">and as explained in the discourses of the Tzemach Tzedek,</t>
    <t s="5">the connection of "the month of oath" to "They administer an oath to him: 'Be righteous.'"</t>
    <t s="6">And perhaps one may add,</t>
    <t s="7">that "in the seventh month" has three interpretations:</t>
    <t s="8">seventh in its simple sense,</t>
    <t s="9">seventh from the word oath</t>
    <t s="10">("the month of oath" as above),</t>
    <t s="11">and seventh from the word satiety,</t>
    <t s="12">as it is brought in the Midrash</t>
    <t s="13">that the interpretation of "in the seventh month" is,</t>
    <t s="14">that it is satiated with everything</t>
    <t s="15">("winepresses within it,</t>
    <t s="16">blessings within it,</t>
    <t s="17">etc.").</t>
    <t s="18">And similarly regarding "They administer an oath to him: 'Be righteous, etc.'",</t>
    <t s="19">as explained in many places</t>
    <t s="20">and also in the discourses of the Tzemach Tzedek,</t>
    <t s="21">that "administer an oath" has three interpretations:</t>
    <t s="22">"administer an oath" in its simple sense,</t>
    <t s="23">and also from the word satiety and from the word seven,</t>
    <t s="24">as will be explained below.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the common theme of oath, satiety, and seven is that an oath binds one's very essence, which is above will, as in the verse "By Myself I have sworn," referring to the level of Atik.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And now, the connection of these three matters</t>
    <t s="2">(oath,</t>
    <t s="3">satiety,</t>
    <t s="4">seven)</t>
    <t s="5">is,</t>
    <t s="6">that the concept of an oath is that it binds one's very essence.</t>
    <t s="7">And as with a simple oath,</t>
    <t s="8">that when a person swears to do something</t>
    <t s="9">(even though now, at the time he swears, he wants to do it,</t>
    <t s="10">so why is the oath needed?),</t>
    <t s="11">it is</t>
    <t s="12">so that even if something occurs that causes him not to want the thing,</t>
    <t s="13">then, by virtue of having sworn to do the thing,</t>
    <t s="14">he will do the thing even against his will.</t>
    <t s="15">And the reason for this is that the concept of an oath is that it binds one's very essence to this,</t>
    <t s="16">the essence of the soul which is above will.</t>
    <t s="17">And similarly above,</t>
    <t s="18">the concept of an oath is as it is written,</t>
    <t s="19">"By Myself I have sworn,"</t>
    <t s="20">"By Myself" means by My very essence.</t>
    <t s="21">And as explained in the discourses,</t>
    <t s="22">that "By Myself" refers to Atik,</t>
    <t s="23">and it is known</t>
    <t s="24">that Atik is the lowest level within the Emanator, which is above the root of the emanated beings.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
